contexts: web assessment form with one free-text field
reading: Comment quality is shaped at three points: the form (what it asks for), the assessor (what they know and whether anyone shows them their own comments) and the moment of writing (soon after the encounter or in an end-of-rotation batch). The retrieved evidence supports changes at each point, with the strongest caution that teaching alone fades (claim c3) and that equity must be watched because women residents receive vaguer comments (claim c4). The committee and the residents are the users of the comments; the chief residents are the measurement system.

nodes.label: Micro-teaching at faculty meetings
nodes.detail: Change idea; fades without reminders (claim c3).

nodes.detail: Specific behaviour, gap and next step (claim c2).

summary: Map joins the form, the assessor and the timing of writing to the actionable comment, with an equity check by gender.
